newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car sales fall for second consecutive month.
newsitem.headline: Japan car sales fall for second consecutive month.

text.p: Car sales in Japan fell in May for the second month in a row, as a sales tax increase continued to bite into consumers' appetite for new cars, an industry body said on Monday.
Vehicle sales, including cars, trucks and buses, fell 9.4 percent in May from a year earlier to 319,940 units, the Japan Automobile Dealers' Association said.
The drop follows a decline of 12.7 percent in April, after Japan's consumption tax rose to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Domestic sales in May by Toyota Motor Corp, Japan's top carmaker, fell 8.1 percent year-on-year to 126,996 units, after a 15.7 percent drop in April.
But a Toyota official said the company expects sales to rebound in the future.
"Domestic orders for our products are recovering. We are not pessimistic because we launched several new models recently," a Toyota spokesman said.
A dealers' association official also expected sales to rebound.
"It's difficult to forecast, but the size of May's decline shrunk from the decline in April and domestic orders are recovering after the initial impact of the sales tax," the official said.
Sales of imported vehicles fell 27.0 percent in May to 22,921 units after a huge 36.8 percent decline in April.
Imported car sales in particular are struggling because they are generally more expensive than Japanese cars, the association official said.
Domestic sales by Honda Motor Co Ltd fell a sharp 14.8 percent in May to 34,762 units after declining just 1.6 percent in April, the company's first fall in 26 months.

"Orders recovered in the middle of May to the same level as last May, but it was tough to post a gain as sales in May last year were high due to strong demand for our recreation vehicles," a Honda spokesman said, adding that the company is likely to register a gain in July or August.

The only one of Japan's five big carmakers to post an increase in domestic sales last month was Mazda Motor Corp, whose sales climbed by 12.7 percent to 20,539 units, after falling 9.9 percent in April.
"Demand for our Demio (recreational vehicle) was strong and we expect another gain this month," a Mazda spokesman said.
Sales by Nissan Motor Co Ltd, Japan's second-biggest carmaker, fell 12.4 percent to 59,361 units in May after a 5.3 percent decline in April.
"We hope to boost our June sales to the same level as last year with sales of new models like the Elgrand," a Nissan spokeswoman said.
Nissan received orders for nearly 7,500 of the multi-purpose vehicles after they went on sale on May 19 with a monthly sales target of 5,000 units.
Mitsubishi Motors Corp's sales fell 10.6 percent to 25,549 units in May, an improvement from April's 24.7 percent drop.
